item.title: BREACH: a New Hacking Game, to Learn How Real Attacks Work
item.description: As a kid I played Activision’s Hacker, then Uplink at 21. BREACH is my take on the genre, with a twist. I wanted to try building a game with Fable, but not one more throwaway clone, so I made one that teaches something. What the game is, why every situation in it comes from real 2025-2026 incidents, why AI makes all of this faster, and how the game itself is built to follow its own lessons, community missions included.

item.title: Paeon: an On-Call Colleague for My Home Server, Who Thinks Before Touching Anything
item.description: The next step after the home network monitoring posts. Why the name (Paeon, the healer of the gods in Homer), why being on call for a home server is the same job as on call at work, only without the laptop, and how Paeon works. Alerts from OpenObserve and Uptime Kuma become incidents, a cheap model filters the noise, a strong model investigates with read-only tools and cites its evidence, my phone gets a Go / No-go button, and a separate process applies only the actions I allowed. Screenshots from the console, the security model and the token economy.
